scope_boundaries: Compact connected Riemann surface and fixed smooth positive background; ordinary models normalized by supremum zero.
Total-variation convergence of polar curvature implies L1 and capacity convergence, including zero non-pluripolar mass.
At a zero-mass limit, full curvature currents converge in total variation with bound twice the model distance.
Weak curvature convergence is equivalent to L1 convergence for normalized potentials, but need not imply capacity convergence even among ideal models.
Capacity convergence does not imply model-metric convergence: moving a full-mass pole has constant distance 2 in area one.
No new higher-dimensional zero-volume continuity, infinite-mass extension or degenerating-background theorem is asserted.
